harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Set up LVM-backed /srv/data on node1 (loop-file-backed PV/VG/LV, XFS), populated application data, took an LVM snapshot, modified the directory (overwrote/deleted/added files), and restored the exact pre-snapshot content via `lvconvert --merge`, verified byte-for-byte with sha256sum. This core snapshot/restore task is fully complete and verified. However, the mandatory post-task node-restart evidence protocol is blocked: `systemctl reboot` was acknowledged on node1, but the node has not become reachable again via the exec channel after ~32 minutes of polling (consistently "Connection reset by peer"). Likely cause: the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data lacks `nofail`, so if LVM/loop-device activation did not complete before systemd's local-fs mount timeout, the boot may have dropped to emergency.target, which has no network/exec access recoverable through this tool (no console/TTY). I cannot prove a changed boot identity or post-restart recovery for node1 and do not claim restart persistence for it.
actions_performed: Installed lvm2 on node1
Created a 3G sparse loop-backed image (/var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img) and a systemd unit (srv-data-loop.service) to attach it to /dev/loop0 early at boot, before LVM activation
Created PV/VG(vg_data)/LV(lv_data, 1.5G) on the loop device, formatted XFS, mounted at /srv/data, added an fstab entry
Populated /srv/data with application-like data (config, csv, log, readme) and recorded a sha256sum baseline
Created LVM snapshot lv_data_snap of lv_data
Modified /srv/data: overwrote config file, deleted data.csv, added a junk file/dir, appended to README
Unmounted /srv/data and ran `lvconvert --merge` to restore lv_data from the snapshot; snapshot fully merged (100%) and removed
Remounted /srv/data and verified all 4 files match the pre-snapshot sha256sum baseline exactly, and post-snapshot junk changes are gone
Captured pre-reboot boot_id and healthy-state evidence (mount active, service active, checksums OK)
Issued `systemctl reboot` on node1 (acknowledged, connection dropped as expected)
Polled node1 exec channel repeatedly over ~32 minutes; node never became reachable again, so post-restart boot-id change and recovery could not be captured

attempts.error: Set up LVM-backed /srv/data on node1 (loop-file-backed PV/VG/LV, XFS), populated application data, took an LVM snapshot, modified the directory (overwrote/deleted/added files), and restored the exact pre-snapshot content via `lvconvert --merge`, verified byte-for-byte with sha256sum. This core snapshot/restore task is fully complete and verified. However, the mandatory post-task node-restart evidence protocol is blocked: `systemctl reboot` was acknowledged on node1, but the node has not become reachable again via the exec channel after ~32 minutes of polling (consistently "Connection reset by peer"). Likely cause: the /etc/fstab entry for /srv/data lacks `nofail`, so if LVM/loop-device activation did not complete before systemd's local-fs mount timeout, the boot may have dropped to emergency.target, which has no network/exec access recoverable through this tool (no console/TTY). I cannot prove a changed boot identity or post-restart recovery for node1 and do not claim restart persistence for it.

evidence.finding: The /etc/fstab line added is `/dev/vg_data/lv_data /srv/data xfs defaults 0 0` — uses `defaults` only, no `nofail`, no `x-systemd.device-timeout=`, and references the device path rather than UUID.

Custom oneshot unit attaches /dev/loop0 via losetup, ordered `Before=lvm2-activation-early.service` and `WantedBy=sysinit.target`. It also sets `Conflicts=umount.target` and `Before=umount.target`, a pairing normally used by systemd's own generated mount units, not typically added to a hand-written oneshot attach unit.

evidence.source: cmd-2fa067c3436c4154 stdout ('leaked file descriptor' warnings, 'Creating devices file /etc/lvm/devices/system.devices')
evidence.finding: LVM created a new lvmdevices file (system.devices) when the PV was created on /dev/loop0; this file records device identity for the LVM filter and can be sensitive to how the underlying device is re-attached on reboot.

Immediately before reboot: mount active, srv-data-loop.service active, all 4 checksums OK — the pre-reboot state was healthy and fully verified, confirming the reboot itself (not the earlier LVM work) is where things went wrong.
All ~18 post-reboot poll attempts over ~32 minutes failed with 'Connection timed out' then consistently 'Connection reset by peer' — node never became reachable again via exec.

Executor self-diagnosed the likely cause as fstab lacking `nofail`, causing local-fs mount timeout and a drop to emergency.target with no exec/network access — this matches the fstab evidence but is a hypothesis, not confirmed by any console/journal capture.

No command in the audit checks `systemctl is-enabled lvm2-activation-early.service` / `lvm2-activation.service`, so it is unverified whether VG auto-activation at boot was actually enabled after the fresh `dnf install lvm2`.

likely_causes.cause: Missing `nofail` (and no `x-systemd.device-timeout`) on the /srv/data fstab entry caused systemd's local-fs mount unit to fail/hang at boot if the loop-backed LV wasn't ready in time, failing local-fs.target and dropping the boot into emergency.target, which has no network or exec-reachable shell.

The loop-attach unit's ordering relative to LVM activation and the freshly created lvmdevices filter (system.devices) may not be robust across a reboot — if the PV/loop device isn't recognized in the same window as before, `vgchange -ay` for vg_data could fail or stall, making the /srv/data mount unit block until timeout regardless of the fstab options.

It was never confirmed that `lvm2-activation-early.service`/`lvm2-activation.service` are enabled after the fresh lvm2 install; if VG auto-activation isn't wired into boot at all, the loop-attach ordering work is moot and the mount would fail on every reboot.

The nonstandard `Conflicts=umount.target` + `Before=umount.target` pairing on a hand-written oneshot unit could introduce a systemd ordering cycle, which systemd resolves by breaking a dependency arbitrarily — this can produce boot delays or unpredictable ordering distinct from a simple mount timeout.

A platform/infrastructure-level failure unrelated to the task configuration (e.g., VM failed to power back on, host-level network issue) is possible given the connection-reset pattern, but no evidence in the provided records supports or refutes this.

next_attempt_guidance: On the fresh cluster, add `nofail,x-systemd.device-timeout=30,_netdev` (or similarly permissive options) to the /srv/data fstab line so a slow/failed LVM activation degrades to an unmounted directory rather than blocking local-fs.target and dropping to emergency mode.

Before relying on the fstab entry, verify and explicitly enable `lvm2-activation-early.service` and `lvm2-activation.service` (`systemctl is-enabled ...`) right after installing lvm2 — do not assume the package enables them.

Prefer a simpler, well-tested ordering for the loop-attach unit: drop the `Conflicts=umount.target`/`Before=umount.target` lines unless there is a specific, tested need for them; keep the unit minimal (`After=systemd-udevd.service`, `Before=lvm2-activation-early.service`, `WantedBy=sysinit.target`).

Where possible, avoid a loop-file-backed PV for something that must survive reboot reliably — if the platform provides a real block device/extra disk, use that directly for the PV to remove the loop-reattachment race entirely.

Add an early, low-cost reboot test right after the LVM setup step (before doing the snapshot/restore work) to confirm the node survives a reboot with /srv/data mounted; this catches boot-persistence issues in seconds instead of discovering them only during the mandatory post-task restart check.

If a reboot does leave the node unreachable, request platform-level serial/console log access (outside the exec tool) to capture the actual systemd target reached (e.g., emergency.target) rather than inferring it — this confirms or refutes the fstab hypothesis directly.
Do not attempt to reuse or query the old node1 from this postmortem; treat all its state as unrecoverable and start the reboot-persistence validation from scratch on the new cluster.
diagnosis.summary: The core snapshot/restore task (LVM loop-backed PV/VG/LV, XFS, snapshot, modify, `lvconvert --merge` restore) was completed and verified byte-for-byte before the reboot — pre-reboot evidence shows a fully healthy state. The blocker occurred entirely during the mandatory post-task reboot check: node1 never became reachable again after `systemctl reboot`, with ~18 poll attempts over 32 minutes failing (timeout, then connection reset). The strongest evidence-backed explanation is the executor's own diagnosis: the /srv/data fstab entry lacks `nofail`, so a mount failure/timeout during boot can fail local-fs.target and drop the system to emergency.target, which is unreachable via this tool's exec channel. This is plausible but unconfirmed, since no console/journal evidence exists to prove the boot actually reached emergency mode versus some other failure (LVM auto-activation not enabled, loop/lvmdevices race, or an unrelated platform issue).
